harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (فإن مع العسر يسرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «مع»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (إن مع العسر يسرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (فإذا فرغت فانصب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (وإلى ربك فارغب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ links the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you ask, then turn with longing to your Lord; and the conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding one.
